summary: Agent 0.36.1 fixes GO-2026-6278 (GHSA-w67g-5rqw-f597), which failed the required go-security check (govulncheck v1.9.0) on every pull request and, at its next run, on main: github.com/gorilla/websocket v1.5.3 generates client frame mask keys with math/rand.Uint32(). No tagged release after v1.5.3 exists; paho.mqtt.golang v1.5.1 and v1.5.2 both require v1.5.3, so the unaffected v1.5.1/v1.5.2 cannot be selected. The agent now requires the commit the advisory names as fixed, v1.5.4-0.20240701034025-d67f41855da4 (go get; go.sum hashes verified against sum.golang.org; go mod tidy changed nothing else, golang.org/x/net stays at v0.62.0, above the v0.26.0 the commit requires). Decision and rejected options in ADR-0126 (accepted by the maintainer). Traced the agent's use (B3): tunnel.go dials the router with websocket.Dialer{HandshakeTimeout, TLSClientConfig} (no Proxy, no NetDial), ws:// or wss:// from the router URL, then ReadMessage/WriteMessage/WriteControl; paho uses the library for MQTT over WebSockets. Inspected the module source diff v1.5.3 -> d67f418 (14 upstream commits): conn.go mask keys now from crypto/rand via io.ReadFull, ioutil -> io; client.go dial refactor that passes the context, for a Dialer without NetDial/NetDialContext still net.Dialer.DialContext, TLS handshake code unchanged; proxy.go now wraps golang.org/x/net/proxy (only reached with Dialer.Proxy set, which the agent does not set); server.go and tests change server code the agent does not use. No change to TLS verification, fingerprint pinning, enrollment, frame format or limits. The wire protocol is unchanged (masking is per frame and transparent to the router).

tests.command: go run golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@v1.9.0 ./... (agent, before and after)
tests.evidence: main 937f6cf: Vulnerability #1 GO-2026-6278, 'Your code is affected by 1 vulnerability from 1 module'; this branch: 'No vulnerabilities found.'

tests.command: go test -count=1 ./... (agent, Linux, golang:1.27.4 container, repository mounted read-only)
tests.evidence: ok github.com/psewar/skirnir/agent 7.3s; with -run Protocol|RouterTLS|Routes|Power -v: 18 tests PASS, among them the tests that open real WebSocket connections through the tunnel (protocol conformance, router TLS incl. the rejected bad-certificate cases, routes, power). A first run with only agent/ mounted failed 7 protocol tests that read ../docs/protocol; not related to the change.

tests.command: gofmt -l . ; go vet ./... ; GOOS=windows go vet ./... ; GOOS=linux go vet ./...
tests.evidence: gofmt prints nothing; vet clean on all three.

tests.command: python test/check_adr_index.py ; python test/check_pinned_references.py ; ruff check .
tests.evidence: ADR index ok: 126 ADRs; pinned references 0 findings; All checks passed.
0 finding(s); added lines reviewed by hand: module versions, hashes, public advisory IDs, ADR text.
The end-to-end suite drives the Python fake agent (test/fake_agent.py), not the Go agent, so it does not reach the changed library; it runs nightly in CI.

limitations: The agent now depends on an untagged upstream commit; the 14 upstream commits were read for the client paths the agent uses, not audited as a whole (server and proxy code are unused by the agent).
Not tested against a real router and node over ws:// and wss://, nor MQTT over WebSockets with a real broker; the Go tests use local httptest servers.
The agent version is set at build time; nodes keep the vulnerable library until the maintainer releases and rolls out agent 0.36.1.
